correctness.rationale: The exact host exponent is −δ²/(B+δ); for sufficiently small δ>0 the next δ is positive and smaller, with δ′=δ−δ²/C+O(δ³). Consequently the exact clock t=C/δ diverges with one-step increment 1+O(1/t), hence t/n→1. Analyticity gives d_n=p_n−p_(n+1)=O(t⁻²) and d_(n+1)−d_n=O(t⁻³). In v=x−2−p the map is h_p(v)+d_n with h_p(v)=(2+p+v)e^(−v)−2−p. The forcing residual over two steps is d_(n+1)−d_n plus O(t⁻²|v|+t⁻³), since ∂p h=O(v) and ∂v h=−1+O(p+|v|). Independent composition gives quadratic coefficient p²(1+p)/2, cubic −1/3+O(p), and quartic O(p); the remainder is uniform on a bounded t v² annulus. Thus w=t v² obeys w′′=w+2w(W*−w)/(3t)+O(t⁻²). Fixed strips near each endpoint have strict inward increments for large t, and the uniform O(1/t) increment cannot leave from the interior. Even-step signs persist and squared error contracts by 1−4w_min/(3t) up to O(t⁻²); divergent total contraction and summable error imply w→W*. Odd/even v ratio tends to −1, while p=O(1/n) is negligible. Both wedges are nonempty and have positive x for sufficiently small initial δ. This yields exactly the original-iteration constants and the two signed limits.
residual_risks: Local one-sided wedges only; no identification of all exceptional or faster orbits. No simulation is used to establish the limits.
